test_changes:
One change, in dsa/tests/lru.prop.test.ts only. The property test now passes an explicit timeout, `PROP_TIMEOUT_MS = Math.max(30_000, PROP.numRuns * 20)`, as the third argument of `it(...)`, with a comment explaining why.

Why: spec §8 (line 1012) requires 10,000 runs nightly. Under Vitest's 5 s default that setting always fails by timeout: 10,000 runs take 32–43 s here. Even the 1,000-run PR setting takes about 3.6 s, which leaves little headroom on a slower CI runner.

Profiling showed the cache itself (including 200,000 checkInvariants calls) is about 0.3 s of the 3.6 s. The rest is the array-filter model and the per-step deep toEqual. No run count, operation, arbitrary or assertion was changed, so the test is not weakened.

dsa/tests/lru.test.ts and dsa/bench/lru.bench.ts are unchanged.

The MEM-02 shape test passed in 1 of 8 runs. get passed in all 8 and pin+unpin stayed at or below 1.62 in all 8. put+evict exceeded the 2x limit in 7 of 8 runs (mean ratios 1.89, 2.09, 2.17, 2.40, 3.58, 3.78, 3.94 and 6.02), on a dev machine at load 4–9 from about 25 parallel agents. benchmark:
Dev machine, not the lab machine: AMD Ryzen 5 7530U (6 cores / 12 threads, 512 KB L2 per core, 16 MB shared L3), Node 24.13.1, Vitest 5.0.1. The machine was heavily loaded by parallel agents. Batches are 1,000 operations. Cells are ns/op, as mean / p50 / p95, median of 3 JSON-recorded runs. Re-run on the lab machine.

- get (hit, Zipf): 62/58/79 at 10^3, 68/63/82 at 10^4, 80/77/100 at 10^5. Mean ratio 1.27–1.44: flat, O(1).
- put+evict (bounded, new keys): 120/117/150 at 10^3, 162/119/242 at 10^4, 229/175/376 at 10^5. Mean ratio 1.89–2.40 against a limit of 2; p50 ratio 1.42–1.84.
- pin+unpin: 65/63/70 at 10^3, 86/80/92 at 10^4, 101/91/132 at 10^5. Ratio 1.15–1.62: flat.
- Array-LRU baseline (touch): 341 ns at 10^3, 2,644 at 10^4, 27,475 at 10^5. It grows 72–139x, the linear O(n) curve.
- Absolute budget: in the three tabulated runs every mean was at most 0.3 µs, within the target of 0.5 µs.
- Bytes/entry, measured including the Map (allocated / used from stats()): 46–59 (27.6 / 27.0) at 10^3; 100 (44.2 / 27.0) at 10^4; 78.6 (35.4 / 27.0) at 10^5. The estimate is 27 B/slot: typed arrays 11 B plus 2 x 8 B array elements, excluding the Map.

The README records all of this in the filled DSA.md template, with a text complexity curve and an explanation of the put+evict growth.
problems:
put+evict failed its shape assertion (mean ratio at most 2, 10^3 to 10^5) in 7 of 8 full-size runs on this dev machine (ratios 1.89–6.02). get and pin+unpin stayed within the limit in all 8 runs. The PR gate at 10^3 and 10^4 passed. I did not weaken the assertion.

My analysis: at steady state each put+evict does three Map operations (a get that misses, a delete, a set), one required [K, V] tuple, and constant sequential slot-array writes to slots i-1, i and i+1. The evicted slot is reused from the free stack, so there is no resize and no loop.

The part that grows with n is V8's Map: about 7 MB at 10^5, well past L2, plus rehashes under delete/insert churn that cause p95 spikes. Raw Map churn alone grew 1.7–3.5x on the same machine. A noise-robust min-p50 comparison still suggested some extra LRU cost at 10^5 (+208 ns against +25 ns at 10^3), which I could not isolate: the machine was at load 5–9 and perf counters are blocked (perf_event_paranoid=4).

It needs a clean lab-machine run. If it still fails there, the README states the reversal trigger: a spec amendment to use S6's IntHashTable instead of Map for integer keys.

Without --expose-gc, measured bytes/entry is null.
